mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL growth > 2% does not correlate with subsequent Fed tightening actions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Real Final Sales of 1% or more signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS growth > 1% does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past month signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 2% does not correlate with subsequent earnings contraction.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past 2 months signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 5% does not correlate with subsequent consumer confidence.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth is below 2%, the real interest rate is high, which signals a restrictive monetary policy and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL growth does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the past month, it signals a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of low UNRATE and high PAYEMS growth does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending increases.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, when GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and Industrial Production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 1%, it signals a weakening supply chain, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ and INDPRO decreases > 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of slow GDPC1 growth and decreasing INDPRO does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.
